_doc: Checked on every Spanish segment (stage 4), on accent-folded lower-case text (foldText: é→e, ñ→n; ¿ ¡ kept). Folding means these rules cannot see a missing accent, and cannot tell voseo from tú where only the accent differs (sabés/sabes): Codex and the adjudicator check those. level fail = the segment must change; level review = a candidate the adjudicator checks in context (good Spanish in other meanings: a subjunctive, a third person, plural ustedes). scope voice = only Evelyn's lines, headlines and reply buttons (kinds bubble, headline, cta); scope all = every segment. No quote exemption in Spanish (pack.json checks.quotedSpan null). Promise rules are review: the line is translated at the English strength and tagged with risk; the operator decides at review. v2 2026-11-20 after Codex's review of the pack.

rules.fix: usted → tú (Evelyn and the buyer always say tú)
usted imperative with a pronoun (dígame, cuénteme, imagínese…) → dime, cuéntame, imagínate, permíteme, siéntete, pregúntate, acuérdate, fíjate, déjame, escríbeme
usted imperative? → disculpa, perdona, oye (fine as a subjunctive: que me perdone)
usted command or question (Haga clic, Ingrese, ¿Desea…?, No se preocupe) → tú (Haz clic, Escribe, ¿Quieres…?, No te preocupes); fine as a subjunctive (para que elija)
vosotros, os, vuestro, tenéis, mirad… → ustedes (Mexico has no vosotros)
voseo (vos, tenés, querés, sos…) → tú forms (tienes, quieres, puedes, eres, vives, piensas, vienes)
fine as plural you (ustedes dos); never as a polite singular
whose is it? the buyer's own X is tu / tus (su is an usted leak); keep su for a third person or for ustedes
coger → tomar / agarrar / elegir (coger is vulgar in Mexico)
Spain usage → Mexican Spanish (computadora, jugo, papas, estacionar…)
Spain usage? → me encanta / lentes (a molar tooth is fine)
Spain 'pincha aquí' → haz clic / toca; in Mexico 'pinche' is vulgar
house style: agregar (añadir is valid, less Mexican)
Spain 'vale' → está bien / de acuerdo / claro ('vale la pena', 'vale $35' are fine)
phone = celular (móvil is fine as 'motive' or an adjective)
drive a car = manejar in Mexico (conducir is fine for 'lead')
house style: enojada / molesta
hacer sentido → tener sentido / tiene lógica
aplicar para (un trabajo) → solicitar / postularte / pedir
llamar para atrás → devolver / regresar la llamada
realizar que → darte cuenta de que
tomar ventaja de → aprovechar (an opportunity) / aprovecharse de (a person)
'excited' about something to come → emocionada / ilusionada
ambiguous (it can mean a double meaning): name what she gets (una segunda lectura, para tu {topic})
water Evelyn blessed = agua bendecida; agua bendita only for church holy water
'in order to' → para / con el fin de
means 'now and then / possibly'; for 'eventually' → con el tiempo / tarde o temprano
means 'currently'; for 'actually' → en realidad
means pregnant; for 'embarrassed' → apenada / avergonzada / me da pena
'support someone' → apoyar / acompañar; soportar = put up with
introduce a person → presentar
'remove' → quitar / eliminar / sacar? (remover = stir up, also fine)
marketing calque → tomar una decisión / actuar, dar el siguiente paso / gratis, sin costo / ahorrar dinero
English-shaped passive? prefer an active verb, but keep the English timing and actor: never make Evelyn the sender the English doesn't name
customer-service register; say it as Evelyn would
essay connector or cliché in a chat line
compare with the English: the same guarantee at the same strength, tagged risk 'claim'; the refund guarantee is "garantía de reembolso"
compare with the English: a promise only where it promises, tagged risk 'claim'; never swap in a different meaning
compare with the English: a certainty claim only where it has one, tagged risk 'claim'
compare with the English: a healing claim only where it says heal, tagged risk 'claim'; never add one under another verb
compare with the English: certainty about the future only if it is that certain
